The throne inside the vineyard — abundance administered with calm competence.
Greed, status hoarding, or wealth that owns its owner.
Does your prosperity serve your life, or has your life become its servant?
A home that works and feeds — care expressed in what is tangible.
Neglect of self, martyrdom of chores, or care given only to others.
When did you last care for yourself as practically as you care for everyone else?
The slowest rider, the surest arrival — devotion to the daily round.
Stagnation, stubborn routine, or persistence aimed at a dead field.
Is your routine a road, or a rut wearing deeper every day?
The student and the coin — a practical ambition ready for its first lesson.
Procrastination, shallow study, or ambition without a teacher.
What skill have you been admiring instead of learning?
The long table — wealth that outlives the hand that built it.
Inheritance disputes, family walls, or wealth without meaning.
What are you building that is meant to outlast you?
The garden, the falcon, the self — abundance enjoyed alone and at ease.
Isolation bought with success, or luxury that hides an empty table.
What would change if you let yourself enjoy what you have built?
Coin after coin, cut with care — mastery built one honest repetition at a time.
Perfectionism, drudgery, or skill sharpened with no purpose in view.
What craft would be yours if you allowed yourself one thousand quiet hours?
Leaning on the hoe, watching the vines — is the harvest worth another season?
Impatience, wasted effort, or quitting one season before the yield.
Is what you are growing worth another season of tending?
The scales and the open hand — giving and receiving in fair flow.
Debt, strings attached, or charity that quietly buys control.
Are you giving freely, or lending at interest you will not name?
Outside the lit window — lack that feels personal but is only weather.
Returning inside, help accepted, or the end of the long cold.
Whose lit window have you been too proud to knock on?
Holding tight to what is yours — security, or the fear of losing it.
Opening the grip, generosity, or releasing what was held too long.
What are you gripping so tightly that it cannot breathe — or be given?
Craft recognized — the builder, the architect and the patron building together.
Sloppy work, dismissed skill, or a team where one person carries all the stone.
Whose skills are you not using because asking would admit you need them?
The dancer keeps both coins in motion — flexibility that holds it together.
Dropped balls, overcommitment, or balance bought at the price of depth.
Which of the things you are juggling would survive being set down?
A seed in an open hand — material opportunity that grows if planted.
Missed opportunity, a seed left unplanted, or value not yet recognized.
What practical opportunity is sitting in your hand unplanted?
Judgment without sentiment — a fair verdict delivered with a steady hand.
Cold tyranny, over-rationalizing feeling, or rules applied without mercy.
Where does your logic protect you from what you already feel?
The honest blade of discernment — clear boundaries spoken without cruelty.
Coldness, cutting words, or honesty that has become a weapon.
Where has your honesty stopped serving truth and started serving distance?
Full charge toward the truth — a mind that will not be slowed or silenced.
Rash speech, burnout, or charging at a battle that was never yours.
Is your pursuit truth, or the feeling of winning?
Eyes open, blade drawn — a curious mind watching before it moves.
Gossip, restless critique, or sharp words without sharp aim.
What have you observed lately that you have not let yourself act on?
The final blow — and the horizon already turning gold behind it.
Rising, recovery, or refusing to accept that the worst is over.
Now that the worst has happened, what is left that was always enough?
The 3 a.m. mind — worry that loops because it is never met in daylight.
Waking from the nightmare, seeking help, or anxiety finally named and faced.
What is the 3 a.m. fear, and what would it say if you asked it to be specific?
Bound but not held — the ropes are loose, the blindfold optional, the door open.
Unbinding, agency reclaimed, or the first step out of a cage that was never locked.
Which of your limitations is a rope you tied yourself?
Quiet strategy — moving alone, with a plan only you fully understand.
Exposure, self-deception, or a scheme that now works against you.
What are you doing in secret that you would not defend in daylight?
Rowing toward a quieter shore — leaving the storm behind, one crossing at a time.
Unresolved baggage, a trip delayed, or dragging the storm into the boat.
What are you carrying into the next chapter that belongs to the last one?
The field is won and empty — count what the victory actually cost you.
Reconciliation, laying down arms, or ending a fight everyone lost.
What is this conflict costing you that you have not put in the ledger?
The knight lies still in the chapel — recovery is strategy, not weakness.
Restlessness, burnout, or returning to battle before the wound closed.
What battle are you re-entering that your body has voted to leave?
The heart pierced by truth — pain that is also information.
Healing, releasing the blade, or reopening a wound that was closing.
What did the pain teach you that comfort never could?
A blindfolded truce — refusing to choose is itself a choice with a cost.
The blindfold slips, a decision surfaces, or the stalemate finally breaks.
What would you know if you stopped refusing to look?
The double-edged truth cuts through fog — a breakthrough that demands honesty.
Blunt insight, weaponized words, or clarity used against yourself.
What truth, once spoken, would cut your problem in half?
The storm held inside a steady man — emotional mastery expressed as calm compassion.
Suppressed feeling, coldness, or manipulation dressed as calm.
Is your calm mastery, or a storm you refuse to feel?
Emotional depth held with steady hands — the listener others heal beside.
Emotional over-absorption, martyrdom of feeling, or intuition clouded by others.
Whose feelings are you carrying as if they were your own?
The romantic offer arrives — a knight who follows the heart, cup extended.
Moodiness, empty gestures, or feelings performed instead of lived.
Are you following your heart, or chasing its reflection?
A fish in a cup — surprise, tenderness and an invitation from the heart.
Emotional immaturity, daydreaming, or a message of the heart ignored.
What is your heart trying to hand you that you keep calling childish?
The rainbow over home — emotional completion shared with the people who matter.
Broken ideals, family fracture, or harmony that is only a picture on the wall.
What does home require from you that you have not been willing to give?
The wish card — deep satisfaction with what you have built and felt.
Smugness, wish without work, or satisfaction that masks an empty seat.
If your wish came true tomorrow, would you recognize yourself in it?
Walking away from a full table — leaving what no longer feeds the soul.
Returning too soon, wanderlust as escape, or abandoning what was not finished.
What are you leaving behind — and is it truly empty, or are you?
Seven visions, one choice — not all of them are real; choose with clear eyes.
Clarity after fog, a decision made, or fantasy finally set down.
Which of your current options would survive contact with reality?
Gifts from the past — memories that nourish rather than imprison.
Living backwards, idealizing what was, or refusing to grow past the garden.
Is the past feeding you, or are you feeding it?
Three cups spilled, two still standing — grief is real, and so is what remains.
Acceptance, forgiveness, or turning back toward what survived.
What remains standing behind you that grief has hidden from view?
A cup offered from the sky while attention is fixed on the ground — the offer is real.
Waking from the fog, new openness, or finally noticing the offered cup.
What opportunity is being offered that your boredom will not let you see?
Joy multiplied by witnesses — celebration that becomes belonging.
Gossip, exclusion, or celebrating with people who drain the room.
Who celebrates your wins with genuine joy — and who only attends?
Two cups raised in equal exchange — a bond built on true reciprocity.
Imbalance, a one-sided pact, or harmony performed but not felt.
In which relationship are you giving what you never asked to receive?
The cup overflows — a new feeling surfaces, asking to be received.
Blocked emotion, withheld love, or a cup poured out before it was drunk.
What feeling is surfacing that you keep calling a problem?
Command earned through vision — a leader who lights the path, not just the torch.
Tyranny, impulsive decree, or charisma without responsibility.
Who are you leading, and have you told them where the fire is taking them?
Radiant self-possession — warmth that leads without demanding.
Jealousy, performative confidence, or fire turned inward.
What would you create if you stopped auditioning for approval?
Full-speed commitment to the adventure — passion with a destination.
Reckless haste, burnout, or charm that promises more than it carries.
Is your speed carrying you toward something, or away from stillness?
The messenger of spark — curious, eager, ready to explore the new.
Restlessness, half-started projects, or novelty used as escape.
What are you most excited to begin — and why have you not begun it?
Carrying more than one person should — the end is near, but the weight is yours.
Delegation, release, or dropping what was never yours to carry.
Which of your burdens would survive being handed to someone else?
Battered but standing — the final wall holds because you refuse to lower it.
Exhaustion, paranoia, or guarding a wall that no longer needs defending.
What is the difference right now between resilience and refusal to rest?
Rapid motion — messages, travel and events arriving all at once.
Delays, misfired signals, or speed without direction.
If everything accelerated tomorrow, are you aimed where you want to land?
Holding the high ground against challengers — defend what you have built.
Overwhelm, siege mentality, or defending a position you no longer believe in.
What are you defending — the idea, or the effort you already spent?
Public recognition of a battle honestly won — earned, not borrowed.
Hollow applause, impostor fear, or victory claimed too early.
What would you let people see if you trusted the win was real?
Healthy friction — competing ideas sharpening each other into a better outcome.
Petty conflict, wasted energy, or a fight that outlived its purpose.
Are you fighting for the outcome or just for the fight?
A milestone reached — pause, celebrate, and let the structure hold you.
Unstable foundations, postponed joy, or celebrating alone what should be shared.
Which recent victory did you forget to celebrate?
Ships already sent — expansion that rewards patient foresight.
Obstacles in delivery, narrow vision, or waiting for others to move first.
What have you set in motion that simply needs your patience now?
The world in hand and the map open — a bold plan forming at the threshold.
Fear of leaving comfort, over-planning, or a horizon ignored.
What is the cost of staying where the map ends?
Pure ignition — a creative spark handed to you, waiting to be claimed.
Delay, blocked energy, or a spark smothered before it caught.
Which idea are you holding at armu2019s length because it would demand you?
The circle closes — a cycle integrated, a self assembled, a journey earned.
Almost there but unfinished; loose ends that block the closing dance.
What would it take to declare this chapter complete?
A call from the deep — rise, account for the past, and answer with your whole self.
Self-condemnation, a refused call, or being judged by an old version of you.
What call have you heard and pretended not to recognize?
Unfiltered light — success, warmth and the simple permission to be seen.
Dimmed confidence, forced optimism, or brilliance kept hidden.
What would you do differently if you were certain of being seen and approved?
The path is lit by moonlight — enough to walk, not enough to be certain.
Fog lifting, fears named, or deception finally visible for what it is.
Which of your fears looks different in daylight?
After the storm, calm water and a clear sky — hope grounded in what survived.
Disillusionment, dimmed faith, or hope without action.
What survived your last storm that you have not yet thanked?
The lightning does not ask permission — what was false collapses so truth can stand.
Averted crisis, delayed reckoning, or rebuilding on the same cracked foundation.
What structure in your life is built on a foundation you already know is false?
The chains are loose — this card names the attachment you have been calling fate.
Breaking free, reclaiming agency, or denying the habit that still owns you.
Which chain around your wrist is loose enough to slip off today?
Opposites blended, not forced — patience that turns tension into medicine.
Imbalance, excess, or rushing a mixture that needed time to settle.
Where in your life are you mixing faster than the mixture can heal?
A necessary ending clears the field — compost for what comes next.
Refusing to let go, dragging a finished chapter into the next one.
What finished chapter are you still carrying as if it were alive?
Suspension as revelation — the view changes only when you stop struggling.
Martyrdom, pointless delay, or sacrifice offered where none was asked.
What would you see if you stopped struggling for one full moment?
Cause and effect meet in the open — an honest verdict, fairly earned.
Bias, avoidance of accountability, or scales weighted by self-deception.
What verdict have you been avoiding by refusing to weigh the evidence?
The wheel turns — what rises now was set in motion long ago; ride the turn.
Resistance to change, bad timing, or clinging to a cycle that has ended.
If this moment is a turning point, what are you being asked to release?
The lantern is lit from within — withdrawal that returns you to yourself.
Isolation without purpose, or a refusal to be found even by those who could help.
What could you hear if you gave yourself one silent day?
The lion is not defeated — it is befriended; softness turns out to be the strongest grip.
Self-doubt, suppressed anger, or force applied where patience was needed.
Where would gentleness win faster than force in your life right now?
Opposing forces harnessed and driven forward by sheer disciplined intent.
Stalled ambition, spinning wheels, or two horses pulling apart.
Which of your inner forces have you been letting drive without reins?
A choice of the heart that aligns two paths — love as decision, not just feeling.
Misalignment, temptation, or a choice postponed until it makes itself.
What choice are you postponing that your heart has already made?
Wisdom passed down — a system, mentor, or ritual that gives shape to belief.
Dogma over truth; institutions whose rules you outgrew but still obey.
Which inherited rule is it time to examine before you follow it again?
Order built stone by stone — boundaries that create safety, not cages.
Rigidity, domination, or a fear of chaos that stifles everything alive.
Where do you need to set a boundary that you have been avoiding?
Growth without force — what you water quietly becomes abundant.
Over-caretaking, creative drought, or dependence dressed as care.
What in your life is asking to be nurtured rather than fixed?
The answer already lives behind the veil; stop asking and start listening.
Ignored instincts, secrets, or a mind flooded with noise instead of signal.
What has your intuition been repeating that logic keeps talking over?
Every tool is already on the table — the moment you commit, reality rearranges.
Trickery or scattered energy; potential leaks into performance instead of creation.
Which tool in your hands are you pretending not to have?
A blank page and a cliff edge — the freedom to begin before you are ready.
Recklessness or paralysis; the leap is postponed and the horizon blurs.
What step would you take today if failure were free?

Fated — until it is carried through

With the Tower, a respected elder or authority.

With the Heart, his affection is true.

With the Birds, written words are discussed.

Hidden knowledge — a secret, a study, or a truth not yet opened to the light.

With the Key, the secret will be unlocked.

Commitment and binding promises — a contract, a vow, or a cycle that ties two things together.

With the Anchor, a commitment that holds.

Love and affection — the heart’s matters rise to the center of the reading.

With the Scythe, the decision cuts fast.
With the Moon, the choice is guided by intuition.
With the Fox, both paths serve someone’s cunning.
A mountain stands in the way — the obstacle is real, but every ascent begins with a single step.
With the Key, the obstacle can be unlocked.
With the Ship, the journey is blocked for now.
With the Sun, the summit is reachable.
The public sphere — gatherings, reputation, and the social circle where you are seen.
With the Birds, public conversation circulates.
With the Bouquet, you are celebrated in company.
With the Clouds, public image blurs.
The long view from the tower — institutions, authority, and the solitude that comes with standing apart.
With the Bear, official power protects.
With the Key, the institution holds the answer.
Loyalty and friendship — the faithful companion who stays when the rest of the world leaves.
With the Heart, a devoted love.
With the Anchor, a friendship that holds.
With the Fox, a false friend flatters.
Change and renewal — the stork migrates, and so will you; the new season is already in flight.
With the Child, a new beginning arrives.
With the House, the household relocates or renews.
With the Ship, change comes from far away.
Clear guidance and quiet hope — the sky is readable again, and the direction is true.
With the Moon, intuition and destiny align.
With the Key, hope finds its answer.
With the Clouds, hope outlasts the fog.
Strength and protective power — a patron, a leader, or your own quiet authority.
With the Tower, institutional power protects.
With the Fish, financial strength grows.
With the Fox, power watches its own interest.
Cunning and self-interest — someone (perhaps you) is being clever; check who profits.
With the Snake, a scheme is coiled nearby.
With the Anchor, a stable job quietly advances.
With the Book, a secret motive is hidden.
Something small and new — a beginning, a child, or a fresh perspective that has not yet learned fear.
With the Bouquet, a new gift or a child brings joy.
With the Stork, a new arrival or birth.
With the Mountain, the new thing grows slowly.
Conversation, a pair, or a flutter of worry — much is said; listen for what is left unsaid.
With the Letter, talk turns into a message.
With the Heart, a couple talks things through.
With the Clouds, gossip confuses the truth.
Conflict or relentless repetition — the same friction returns until its source is named.
With the Fox, the argument hides a lie.
With the Heart, passion and friction mix.
With the Scythe, the quarrel cuts ties.
A sudden cut — one clean decision that severs what cannot continue and harvests what is ripe.
With the Tree, health demands an urgent cut.
With the Coffin, the break is final.
With the Crossroads, the cut forces a choice.
A gift, a compliment, or beauty offered freely — accept it without calculating the price.
With the Heart, a gift becomes affection.
With the Ring, a proposal of devotion.
An ending and a long rest — what is over must be laid down before anything new can begin.
With the Stork, an ending opens into change.
With the Key, closure unlocks a door.
With the Stars, the end heals into hope.
A detour, a temptation, or a clever rival — the straight path is not the one being offered.
With the Fox, flattery hides a trick.
With the Key, you will see through the ruse.
With the Whip, an argument coils back.
Confusion and uncertainty gather — wait for the fog to thin before you decide.
With the Sun, clarity breaks through.
With the Moon, doubts deepen before they lift.
With the Stars, hope survives the storm.
Slow organic growth and health — what is rooted deep grows strong over years, not days.
With the Coffin, a cycle of health ends and another begins.
With the Mountain, growth is blocked.
Home, family and the private sphere — safety, roots, and the structures that shelter your life.
With the Stork, the household changes.
With the Mice, something at home quietly drains.
With the Ring, family bonds are sealed.
Movement across distance — travel, trade, or a longing that pulls you toward something far away.
With the Anchor, a voyage ends in a safe harbor.
With the Rider, a trip is announced.
With the Mountain, the journey is delayed.
A small stroke of luck and a lighter heart — seize the moment while the door stands open.
With the Sun, luck grows into success.
With the Mice, luck slips away if you wait.
With the Rider, good news arrives by chance.
News and momentum riding in — a message, a visitor, or a fresh impulse that sets things moving.
With the Letter, the message arrives in writing.
With the Clover, lucky news comes quickly.
With the Ship, news arrives from far away.
The ancestral land — inheritance, home ground, and what outlives a single life.
The rune of the family estate: land held across generations, a seat at the long table.
Exile, inheritance squandered, or walls that keep kin out.
Daybreak — the turn of night into day, the paradox that completes itself.
The rune of dawn: the moment the long night yields to the long day.
The seed’s silence — potential stored, the energy of what is about to become.
Ing’s rune: the god of the fertile earth, the stored seed of the coming year.
Water and the deep — intuition that moves like the tide, under and around reason.
The rune of the sea-road: voyages, dreams and what the depths remember.
Drowning, illusion, or feeling that floods the shore.
The human — self-knowledge and the kinship that makes an individual a people.
The rune of humankind: the self seen in the eyes of the clan.
Self-doubt, isolation, or the crowd drowning the self.
The horse and rider — two wills moving as one, progress built on mutual trust.
The rune of the mounted pair: the bond between rider and steed, partner and partner.
Mistrust, broken pace, or a partnership pulling in two directions.
The birch-goddess — birth, growth and the quiet nurture that makes things flourish.
The rune of the birch grove: spring’s first green and the goddess of new life.
Stalled growth, neglect, or a birth refused its season.
Tyr’s rune — the hand offered into the wolf’s mouth for the sake of the oath.
The rune of the one-handed god: justice that costs the judge something.
Injustice, broken oaths, or victory won without honor.
The sun — unstoppable light, will aimed true, victory that does not apologize.
The sun-rune: the wheel of light that drives the long northern day.
The elk’s antlers — protection raised, the ward that turns harm aside.
The ward-rune: antlers lifted against the wolf, the warning of the marsh-bird.
Exposure, dropped defenses, or a shield carried for the wrong war.
The lot-cup and the hidden — what chance decides and what the runes keep secret.
The rune of the thrown lots: fate read in the fall of carved wood.
Secrets kept too long, or luck that runs against you.
The yew — the world-tree’s endurance, death and rebirth braided into one root.
Odin’s rune of the yew bow: the spine of the worlds, flexible and unbroken.
The year’s wheel turning — what was sown in its season returns in its own time.
The harvest-rune: the farmer’s year, where nothing ripens before its month.
Ice — a frozen pause in which nothing moves and everything waits.
The rune of the frozen river: stillness so deep it becomes its own season.
Need-fire and necessity — constraint that teaches what comfort never could.
The rune of necessity: the cold that teaches a long winter’s patience.
Hunger, despair, or resistance to a lesson need is teaching.
Hail out of a clear sky — sudden disruption that clears the field for what comes next.
The hail-rune: the storm that flattens the harvest and the seed it leaves behind.
Joy that comes from belonging — kinship, shared work and the peace of the tribe.
The rune of the clan’s gladness — prosperity shared around one hearth.
Loneliness, joy postponed, or belonging bought too cheap.
The gift and the counter-gift — every bond is an exchange kept alive by both hands.
The rune of hospitality: no gift without return, no bond without balance.
The torch of skill — knowledge that illuminates and the craft that shapes the dark.
The smith’s fire: the rune of the forge, the workshop and the skill of the hand.
Extinguished light, raw potential unshaped, or fever without direction.
The ride and the road — movement with a rhythm, the journey as much as the arrival.
The wagon-rune: right motion in right order, the wheel that turns and returns.
Delay, wrong turns, or a journey forced off its road.
The mouth of Odin — inspired speech, signals, and the message carried on the wind.
The rune of the Allfather’s breath — poetry, runes and the advice of elders.
Lies, bad counsel, or words that outrun their meaning.
The thorn and the hammer — a reactive strike that protects the boundary.
Thor’s rune of the giants’ thorn: defense that stings whatever pushes too far.
Hostility, hasty blows, or a threat you refuse to see.
Untamed strength and the body’s own will — the aurochs that cannot be domesticated.
The wild ox of the northern meadows — power that comes from the earth, not from training.
Weakness, missed force, or strength turned against itself.
Movable wealth and raw energy — prosperity that must keep flowing to stay alive.
Freyr’s first rune: the cattle-wealth a free farmer could count, and the fire that keeps a homestead alive.
Loss, greed, or energy burned faster than it is earned.
The Mystic — the part of you that absorbs the mood and dreams it back softer.
Escapism, blurred boundaries and a quiet habit of casting yourself as the one who can only endure.
Merging and empathic; loves through atmosphere and imagination, and needs boundaries to keep the tenderness real.
Art, healing, music and contemplative work where sensitivity is the instrument.
The Reformer — the part of you that questions the crowd and rebuilds the system for the people outside it.
Detachment, contrarianism and keeping everyone at a principled distance.
Friendship-first and unconventional; needs intellectual freedom and a partner who is also a comrade.
Technology, science, activism and networks where the future is being designed.
The Architect — the part of you that respects limits and builds something that outlasts the mood.
Coldness, workaholism and a fear of failure that turns discipline into self-punishment.
Committed and slow; shows love through reliability and long-term plans rather than sudden declarations.
Management, engineering, institutions and legacy work where the long game is the reward.
The Seeker — the part of you that needs the bigger story and will travel to find the sentence that fits.
Dogma, escape and promising more adventure than can be delivered.
Adventurous and honest; needs room to roam and a partner who is also a fellow traveller.
Teaching, travel, publishing and philosophy where the horizon is the point.
The Alchemist — the part of you that goes all the way down and returns with something worth keeping.
Control, secrecy and resentment held long past its usefulness.
All-in and private; tests trust before it gives it, then protects the bond with fierce loyalty.
Research, crisis work, finance and psychology where the hidden layer is the real subject.
The Diplomat — the part of you that weighs both sides before it commits and finds the fair form.
Indecision, people-pleasing and avoiding conflict until the choice is made by default.
Romantic and partnership-minded; flourishes with someone who treats the relationship as a shared work of art.
Law, design, negotiation and partnership where the human interface is the work.
The Artisan — the part of you that serves by noticing what can be made precise.
Perfectionism, self-criticism and control disguised as helpfulness.
Attentive and practical; shows love through small acts of repair and needs appreciation for the invisible work.
Analysis, health, editing and systems where accuracy is the craft.
The Sovereign — the part of you that creates warmth by taking the stage and giving it back to the room.
Pride, needing applause and becoming rigid when the audience looks elsewhere.
Generous and loyal; wants to be seen and celebrated, and gives the same spotlight in return.
Performance, leadership and creative direction where a personal signature is the product.
The Guardian — the part of you that remembers who was there and builds a home out of that loyalty.
Over-attachment, moodiness and expressing needs indirectly so they can never be refused out loud.
Protective and nurturing; bonds through shared history and needs reassurance that the home is mutual.
Care, hospitality, family business and heritage work where feeling is part of the competence.
